lesson_title: The Where-Rule and the Who-Rule: GDP and GNI
hook_text: Two questions about one street — and they give two different answers.
clip_script: Suppose your street totals up everything it produced this year. Question one — the WHERE-rule: what was made ON this street? That's GDP. The outsider's bottle store counts fully — it stands here. The street's daughter working in Cape Town doesn't — her work happens there. GDP measures the PLACE: the street as a machine. Question two — the WHO-rule: what did the street's PEOPLE earn, wherever they earned it? That's GNI. Now the daughter counts — she's ours, and her salary flows home. And the bottle store partly falls away — its profits drive off to the owner's town every evening. Here's the part nobody tells you: the GAP between the two numbers is the real story. Big GDP, smaller GNI — the machine is here, the keeping is elsewhere. That's roughly South Africa's shape. People working out, wages flowing home — GNI above GDP. That's Lesotho's shape. Two rules. Two numbers. One story hiding in the gap.
visual_style: A stylised aerial street that splits into two glowing overlays — a WHERE grid highlighting every building in place, then a WHO web tracing salary lines home from far away — ending with two number columns and the gap between them pulsing.
pacing: Two clean question-beats with matching visuals, accelerating into the gap reveal, cold stop on the final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to read the gap.
